text.p: The San Francisco 49ers Wednesday said they signed star quarterback Steve Young, the NFL's top passer five times in the last six years, to a new contract. Terms of the deal were not disclosed.

Young, who turns 36 in October, was scheduled to earn $4.5 million in the final year of his current contract. His designation as the team's "franchise player" will be allowed to expire at the end of the season.
Young's deal follows those recently signed by quarterbacks Brett Favre of Green Bay and Mark Brunell of Jacksonville.
The Packers rewarded Favre with the richest annual contract -- a seven-year deal worth up to $48 million -- and the Jaguars signed Brunell to a five-year contract worth $30.5 million.
Young battled through a tough 1996 season where he suffered groin, rib and head injuries behind a beleagured offensive line and missed four games.
But despite the injuries, Young finished as the NFL's top passer. He completed 67.7 percent of his passes (214-of-316) for 2,410 yards and 14 touchdowns with six interceptions.

Young was hampered by sore ribs in San Francisco's 35-14 playoff loss to the Packers. He started the game with a flak jacket, but was able to play just two offensive series' in the first quarter before departing.
Young, a two-time NFL Most Valuable Player, threw a Super Bowl record six touchdown passes in San Francisco's 49-26 win over San Diego in January of 1995.
Young officially succeeded Joe Montana as the 49ers' starting quarterback when Montana was injured in 1991.
